Breaking: Tesla rolls out Robotaxi in San Antonio with a 274 sq mi geofence on paper

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1082 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is launching its Robotaxi service in San Antonio, its eighth city, with a launch geofence covering about 274 square miles.
  • But if Tesla’s recent maps are any guide, a massive chunk of that area won’t be bookable.
  • Tesla’s official Robotaxi account made the announcement just after midnight local time: “Robotaxi available in San Antonio starting tomorrow, 5am.” It came with a map of the “launch geofence,” a large polygon that runs from Loop 1604 on the north side down to just south of downtown.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is launching its Robotaxi service in San Antonio, its eighth city, with a launch geofence covering about 274 square miles. That’s the biggest day-one map Tesla has ever posted, and more than four times the size of Waymo’s San Antonio service area.

But if Tesla’s recent maps are any guide, a massive chunk of that area won’t be bookable. In Austin, an independent check found the Robotaxi app only accepted pickups and drop-offs in about 59% of the zone Tesla advertises.

Tesla’s official Robotaxi account made the announcement just after midnight local time: “Robotaxi available in San Antonio starting tomorrow, 5am.” It came with a map of the “launch geofence,” a large polygon that runs from Loop 1604 on the north side down to just south of downtown.

In a recent development, robotaxi Tracker, which measures operator maps and logs fleet sightings, puts the zone at 274 square miles. That covers about 1.0 million residents (51% of the metro) and 721,000 jobs. San Antonio International Airport sits inside the polygon, but it isn’t served.

Waymo started driverless rides in San Antonio in February with more than 60 square miles and opened to all riders in October, airport trips included. Robotaxi Tracker currently lists Waymo’s San Antonio area at 59 square miles.

What Tesla didn’t say is how many cars will cover its 274 square miles. As of Monday morning, Robotaxi Tracker hadn’t logged a single Tesla Robotaxi in San Antonio.

In a recent development, the launch landed the same day Tesla expanded Austin again. The tracker now measures Tesla’s Austin zone at 443 square miles, up 178 square miles since mid-September.

Sources indicate that we’ve seen this movie. Last month, Tesla expanded its Houston geofence into the shape of a rocket, and within two days the creator of Robotaxi Tracker found the app refusing downtown pickups inside it.

Since then, Koby Pierce, who tracks Tesla’s service on X, has done the tedious work of checking city after city. He searched thousands of real addresses in the Robotaxi app on an emulator and mapped only the ones where Tesla allows a pickup or drop-off, then compared that with the map Tesla advertises. Here’s the share of Tesla’s advertised land area that actually works:.

Austin's dropoff/pickup Geofence is ~41% smaller than advertised.Seems mostly the East side of town is inaccessible. Unsure the cause. Any ideas?Dallas is next and should be done by noon tomrrow. pic.twitter.com/WvU99sJlJh.

Austin is the one that matters. It’s Tesla’s flagship market, with 453 unsupervised vehicles in service according to Robotaxi Tracker. Yet about 41% of the advertised map Pierce tested, mostly on the east side of town, wouldn’t take a ride request. Pierce points to railroad crossings as a big factor in several cities, which lines up with the strange downtown routing we saw in Houston.

In a recent development, to be fair, Pierce notes Waymo is next on his list, and he expects “they’re no better.” Robotaxi Tracker already had to trim Waymo’s Orlando area last month after finding the airport, inside Waymo’s published map, wasn’t selectable. We’ll look at those numbers when they’re out. But it doesn’t change what Tesla is doing with San Antonio today.

Recent findings suggest that credit where it’s due. A 274-square-mile launch in a upcoming city is progress, and Tesla now runs unsupervised rides in eight cities. At the start of this year, it had no unsupervised rides anywhere.

Recent findings suggest that but we need to stop taking Tesla’s geofence numbers at face value, and that includes us. We used Tesla’s 254-square-mile figure for Houston, and it turned out to be overstated. In all six cities Pierce has checked, the real service area is between 59% and 78% of what Tesla posts. In Austin and Miami, it’s about 60%.

It has been revealed that so the honest way to read the San Antonio announcement is “up to 274 square miles.” In practice, expect something closer to 160 to 210 square miles, with an unknown number of cars, and the airport already off the table. That’s still bigger than Waymo’s 59 square miles in the city.

Recent findings suggest that these maps are mostly fiction. I live inside the Houston map but the app says I am outside. If you drive to where the app allows, no vehicles are ever available. Waymos are a routine site and are available on a short notice. This is smoke and mirrors to shore up the firm value ahead of the SpaceX merger.

According to recent reports, the problem is that square miles are the metric Tesla fully controls. Drawing a polygon costs nothing, and the numbers were all over X within hours of the post. Cars per square mile, wait times, and rides completed are much harder to inflate, and nationally Waymo still runs over 4,000 driverless vehicles to Tesla’s 666, per Robotaxi Tracker.

I still consider this a small pilot by any standard, and safety remains the bottleneck. Tesla is still forcing riders through hour-long rides that should take 15 minutes because they have to take routes that avoid areas that Tesla can’t safely navigate without supervision.

Until that’s fixed, robotaxi won’t be able to meaningfully scale beyond these limited demonstrations in geo-fenced areas.

Robotaxi or not, most EV charging still happens at home, and pairing it with rooftop solar can cut your cost per mile to nearly zero. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. One lucky meme coin trader made bank as Grand Theft Auto 6 launched worldwide, turning $300 into over $200,000 after early footage of the game sent degens flocking from one unofficial token to another.

The trader bought $307 worth of the DCTY token shortly after it launched in October and has sold their bag for $202,278, according to DEX Screener, a profit of almost 66,000%.

Early indications had pointed to GTA 6 featuring an in-game meme coin—with, it's worth stressing, no actual blockchain element—called "DacityCoin," which appeared in the official launch trailer on a plane with a wing walker setting off a smoke bomb on top of it.

It was later linked to leaked gameplay of an mission which appeared to show game protagonist Lucia parachuting as a stunt to attract investment to DacityCoin.

Sources indicate that amid this hype, per DEX Screener, a real-world and unofficial DacityCoin rolled out using the Solana launchpad Pump.fun. It first peaked at a $4.95 million market capitalization, following the launch trailer's release, before tanking 93% to $343,620 as hype faded.

With GTA 6 set to launch within a matter of hours of publication, the token drew renewed attention, propelling it to a upcoming all-time high of $10.8 million Wednesday. Unfortunately for investors, GTA 6's staggered global release means that some gamers are already playing it—and footage started to spread which suggested the Solana token's ticker was wrong.

The result was a rollercoaster of volatility, with the DacityCoin token now sitting at a market cap of around $800,000.

Gameplay footage from Brazilian streamer Combo Infinito suggests that the in-game token is called DacityCoin, with the ticker DCTY.

https://t.co/kgefwOzGCH pic.twitter.com/LEDrcP7gve.

— Dusty (@guidustyy) November 18, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that that propelled another Solana token with a seemingly accurate name and ticker sprang into action. DCTY's previous all-time high market cap was just $54,000 before the ticker was revealed, and it set a new high of over $12 million after footage of the game appeared to confirm that its ticker matched the in-game token. It is now trading at a market cap of around $10 million.

The game itself appears to be somewhat inconsistent in its naming of the in-game token. During the trailer, it appeared to be spelled "DacityCoin" as one word, however, the subtitles in the leak show it spelled as "Dacity coin," two words. Similarly, the company behind the in-game token is AudaCity, but leaks show three different spellings: Auda City, AudaCity, and Auda-City.

It is worth stressing: Rockstar has not explicitly confirmed that a meme coin will be featured in-game, and any real-world token has no official links to GTA 6 or its creators. Footage is still being released, and absolute confirmation of the in-game token's involvement is still being established.

Sources indicate that those still holding the now-tanking DacityCoin are hoping things will turn around. Mike Lerro, the community takeover lead for DacityCoin, shrugged off any chance that the unofficial token's name and ticker are wrong.

Recent findings suggest that "No, bro. DacityCoin and AudaCity are in the game. Yes or no?" When Decrypt suggested the ticker might be wrong, he replied, "It doesn't matter… Okay and ? The person who creates it will dump on you then it goes to zero. Who's gonna [do the community takeover]? No one.".

According to recent reports, "DACITYCOIN AND AUDACITY ARE IN THE GAME," Lerro wrote in the meme coin's Telegram. "NOTHING ELSE MATTERS.".

According to recent reports, "It's so crazy, it'll correct itself," Lerro said in an emergency Telegram group chat call. "I hope so," an investor replied.

Recent findings suggest that ripple's RLUSD stablecoin led the daily ranking of stablecoin inflows into decentralized finance (DeFi), according to Token Terminal data that RWA Foundation shared on X. The DeFi total value locked (TVL) of Ripple's stablecoin grew by $22.3 million over 24 hours, and Tether added $21.6 million. RWA Foundation titled its chart "Ripple led stablecoin DeFi growth.".

Paxos, Open Standard and Societe Generale followed with $7.8 million, $4 million and $1.2 million, respectively. World Liberty, United Stables, MetaMask, Tori and Liquity each added less than $700,000 over the same period.

Sources indicate that about $2.8 billion worth of RLUSD is in circulation, compared with about $180 billion worth of Tether's USDT. Tether's stablecoin is still more than 60 times bigger than RLUSD.

Ripple introduced RLUSD in December 2024. In mid-September 2026, RLUSD supply passed $2.44 billion, and about $1.38 billion of it was on Ethereum. About $1.05 billion was on the XRP Ledger, Ripple's home network. On Ethereum, the stablecoin is used in DeFi pools on Aave V3, Curve and Morpho.

RLUSD is issued by Standard Custody & Trust under the supervision of the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS), and its reserves are held at custodian bank BNY. In the fall, RLUSD received a Moody's rating and was listed on Coinbase and Robinhood, and Ripple received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch Ripple National Trust Bank.

Ripple has also integrated RLUSD with payment providers Arf, Convera and Cross River Bank, and the stablecoin is now used in dollar settlements between companies.

According to recent reports, in a CNBC interview on Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse called blockchain-based transactions "a wave of emerging technology." "I think 10 years from now you'll see blockchain implemented across our financial infrastructure," he remarked.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that S&P Global Ratings assigned a score of 5 to Tether’s USDT, the weakest in its five-point stablecoin stability scale.
  • According to recent reports, this was mainly because there was a growing proportion of higher-risk assets in Tether’s reserves.
  • Notably, the agency also warned that a significant decline in their market value could erode Tether’s reserve surplus and potentially leave it undercollateralized.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that S&P Global Ratings assigned a score of 5 to Tether’s USDT, the weakest in its five-point stablecoin stability scale. What’s more surprising here is the fact that the assessment, which was published on the 18th of November, 2026, has remained unchanged since November 2025.

According to recent reports, this was mainly because there was a growing proportion of higher-risk assets in Tether’s reserves. According to S&P Global, these assets accounted for 28% of circulating USDT as of the 30th of September 2026, compared with 24% in 2025.

Notably, the agency also warned that a significant decline in their market value could erode Tether’s reserve surplus and potentially leave it undercollateralized.

That said, Tether’s reserve composition has also shifted over the past year, with gold holdings rising from $12.9 billion in September 2025 to $19 billion in September 2026. Meanwhile, the company also added $4.2 billion in publicly traded equities, while its Bitcoin holdings declined from $9.9 billion to $8.4 billion.

In a recent development, yet, despite the growing exposure to riskier assets, Tether reported $191.45 billion in reserves against $183.50 billion in liabilities as of the 30th of September. This in turn left a reserve buffer of approximately $7.95 billion and a collateralization ratio of 104.3%, up from 103.9% in 2025.

Still, above all of this, USDT traded close to its $1 peg over the past year, while its market capitalization grew from $158 billion to approximately $184 billion between September 2025 and September 2026.

However, according to a recent AMBCrypto report, Tether’s market capitalization dropped by $6.6 billion over the course of sixty days, ending on the 7th of November.

Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Home » Exchanges » Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default.
  • AI-powered trading tools are gradually becoming the default interface for Web3 trading, fresh research reveals.
  • A fresh report from Bitrue Research Institute tracks how trading bots have shifted from specialist software for technical customers into everyday infrastructure across crypto markets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Exchanges » Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default.

AI-powered trading tools are gradually becoming the default interface for Web3 trading, fresh research reveals.

A fresh report from Bitrue Research Institute tracks how trading bots have shifted from specialist software for technical customers into everyday infrastructure across crypto markets.

The research paper combines public GitHub data on open-source projects, a survey of Bitrue people, and profiles of eight active bots to show where automation is heading.

Sources indicate that public GitHub activity shows a clear change in focus. Latest repositories describing themselves as “trading agents” jumped from 110 in 2024 to 1,133 in 2025 and reached 6,121 through November 15, 2026, more than five times the prior year’s total.

Classic crypto trading bot projects also grew sharply, rising from 551 in 2024 to 2,399 in 2025 (a 4.4× increase) with another 2,948 created so far in 2026.

The longest-running open-source tools still dominate stars: Freqtrade (56,933), Hummingbot (21,231), Jesse (8,807), and OctoBot (6,951).

An industry survey of 3,708 crypto traders published by MEXC in October 2026 found that 84.8% had used AI for research or trading in the previous six months, with 53.1% doing so at least weekly.

Among AI customers, 34.6% had used an exchange’s own strategies or bots and 17.1% had connected an external agent.

On one major multi-exchange platform, average daily bot launches rose 29% from July to September 2026, reaching 862 per day, with real-fund launches up 36% and DCA bots up 80%.

The report identifies five structural changes:.

In Bitrue’s survey of users who had not yet tried an AI trading bot, concern about losses and risk control was the top reason for hesitation (45.5%). Other common reasons included not trading futures yet (27.3%) and simply not knowing the feature existed (22.7%).

Willingness to let AI trade rose from 55% when only notifications were offered to 71.8% when limits on funds, positions, leverage, and losses were in place. Only 6.5% of respondents stated they would allow AI to control more than half their account.

According to recent reports, among non-customers, the most requested first steps were a clearer explanation of what the bot does (27.3%) and a trial reward for the first trade (22.7%). Half of those who had not tried an AI bot mentioned they were ready to do so; another 36.4% wanted to learn more first.

According to recent reports, owners who had already tried Bitrue AI most often cited time saved from watching charts, automatic execution, and market analysis as the main benefits. Requests for improvement centered on more trading pairs, flexible parameters & alerts tied to indicators such as RSI.

The report profiles eight systems that illustrate different approaches:.

According to recent reports, AI automation continues to expand, but adoption still hinges on control. Crypto traders want to see why a strategy was chosen, know the maximum loss, test it first, and understand connection security and costs.

Tools that explain their reasoning, enforce user-set boundaries, and allow small or reversible starts are the ones positioned to convert interest into regular use. The report does not forecast specific outcomes beyond these observed trends.

The numbers show both rapid builder activity and cautious but growing trader demand. The gap between the two is being closed by guardrails, explanations, and simpler interfaces rather than by handing full control to AI.

Tech Report: LiveWire just showed off its biggest electric motorcycle lineup yet

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1064 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that liveWire has spent the last few years expanding beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.
  • I stopped by the LiveWire booth at EICMA 2026, where the organization had everything from its new lightweight S4 Honcho models to the freshly acquired DUST electric dirt bikes – plus STACYC’s electric balance bikes for the youngest riders.
  • It’s quite a spread, and perhaps more importantly, it paints a picture of a tech giant that increasingly wants to have an electric two-wheeler for just about every stage of a rider’s life.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that liveWire has spent the last few years expanding beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off. But seeing the organization’s latest machines all together at EICMA in Milan really drives home just how much broader LiveWire’s ambitions have become.

I stopped by the LiveWire booth at EICMA 2026, where the organization had everything from its new lightweight S4 Honcho models to the freshly acquired DUST electric dirt bikes – plus STACYC’s electric balance bikes for the youngest riders.

It’s quite a spread, and perhaps more importantly, it paints a picture of a tech giant that increasingly wants to have an electric two-wheeler for just about every stage of a rider’s life.

I also had a chance to spend several hours test-riding the S4 Honcho Street in Milan, so be on the lookout for that article and video to experience it with me.

But for now, let’s see what was at the LiveWire booth.

Perhaps the most crucial bikes at the booth were the S4 Honcho models, LiveWire’s new lightweight and lower-cost electric motorcycles.

It has been revealed that the production S4 Honcho Street made its European debut at EICMA alongside the dirt-oriented S4 Honcho Trail. The Trail version recently began reaching customers in the US, with the Street now en route to dealerships, and European sales are beginning around the EICMA launch.

Industry observers note that these bikes represent a significant departure from LiveWire’s earlier strategy. Instead of trying to compete directly with full-size gasoline motorcycles on outright performance, the Honcho platform is aimed at riders looking for something smaller, simpler, and more approachable.

And now the family is getting even bigger.

Also on display was the fresh S4 Honcho Skate, making its first public appearance.

The Skate is planned for 2027 and further expands the modular Honcho platform with a stripped-down, playful design.

For those who have followed H-D’s electric ambitions for as long as I have, you might even remember the original Harley-Davidson electric moped prototype that seems to have served as inspiration for the Honcho Skate’s design.

Seeing the various Honcho versions together also makes LiveWire’s strategy with the platform much clearer. Rather than creating one small electric motorcycle, the company is building an entire family around the concept.

The other major attraction at LiveWire’s booth was the DUST lineup.

LiveWire acquired the assets of DUST Moto earlier this year, bringing the lightweight electric dirt bike tech giant under its umbrella. EICMA marked the first public showing of the production-intent DUST Hightail under LiveWire ownership.

Sources indicate that the Hightail had already generated plenty of interest before the acquisition as a lightweight, high-performance electric dirt bike. Now we’re getting our first look at how that machine fits into LiveWire’s broader looks.

The manufacturer is targeting a 2027 introduction for the production Hightail.

LiveWire also showed the new DUST Spur, another model planned for 2027 and intended to expand the newly formed DUST family.

The DUST acquisition is particularly interesting because it gives LiveWire an immediate foothold in the rapidly growing lightweight electric off-road motorcycle space without having to develop an entirely newly introduced platform from scratch.

In what could be a hint at faster charging to come, there was an interesting S2 Alpanista Corsa motorcycle that had been outfitted with a NACS plug and DC fast-charging capabilities.

LiveWire claimed a 20-80% charge in under 10 minutes, which would revolutionize the ability to do long-distance motorcycle touring, or just make it more convenient to get a quick charge and head back to your apartment.

There’s on word on whether the concept will make it to production, but the specs are enticing!

The most interesting part of LiveWire’s EICMA display may not have been any individual motorcycle, but rather what happens when you stand back and look at the entire booth.

Industry observers note that on one end you’ve got STACYC electric balance bikes. LiveWire says the brand has already introduced more than 250,000 riders to two wheels.

Recent findings suggest that then you’ve got the lightweight S4 Honcho family. Above that sit the DUST machines for more serious off-road riding, while LiveWire’s existing S2 motorcycles continue to cover the higher-performance street end of the spectrum.

That’s becoming something of an electric two-wheeler ladder.

A kid can theoretically start on a STACYC, graduate into increasingly capable electric two-wheelers, and eventually wind up on a proper electric motorcycle – all within the same corporate family.

And that feels particularly relevant at a show like EICMA, where much of the motorcycle industry is still trying to figure out exactly where electric motorcycles fit.

LiveWire seems increasingly convinced that the answer isn’t simply to build electric replacements for existing gasoline motorcycles.

Instead, the company is spreading out into categories where electric drivetrains can create different kinds of motorcycles altogether.

I’ve been following LiveWire’s evolution for years, and the tech giant standing in front of me at EICMA looks considerably different from the one that started out selling a single expensive flagship electric motorcycle.

The big, high-performance bikes are still key, but machines like the S4 Honcho and DUST Hightail are arguably more interesting to me because they can bring entirely different riders into electric motorcycling.

Recent findings suggest that they’re smaller. They’re simpler. And perhaps most importantly, they’re targeting the kind of fun, accessible riding that doesn’t require superbike levels of performance.

There’s still plenty we need to learn about several of these upcoming models, particularly final specifications and pricing for the 2027 machines.

But seeing the Honcho, Honcho Skate, Hightail, Spur, and STACYC machines together at EICMA makes one thing pretty clear: LiveWire isn’t just trying to sell a few electric motorcycles anymore.

It’s trying to build an entire electric two-wheeler ecosystem.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that russia has finally opened its crypto market for retail customers as its central bank today enabled trading in Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT for the general public.
  • The newly introduced regulation, revealed by the Bank of Russia last week, took effect today, Nov.
  • In a recent development, the announcement expands access to regulated crypto trading in the country and connects the assets with TradFi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that russia has finally opened its crypto market for retail customers as its central bank today enabled trading in Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT for the general public. With the law signed by President Vladimir Putin, the Bank of Russia officially rolled out BTC, ETH, and USDT for public trading on domestic exchanges, beginning Nov. 17, 2026.

The newly introduced regulation, revealed by the Bank of Russia last week, took effect today, Nov. 17. The move allows individual customers to purchase these assets through intermediaries, including brokers, exchanges, and authorized crypto marketplaces. This means ordinary investors can now buy up to 300,000 rubles ($3,700) in a year through a single broker, exchange, or asset manager, after passing a mandatory test.

In a recent development, the announcement expands access to regulated crypto trading in the country and connects the assets with TradFi. This allows non-qualified investors to buy and trade BTC, ETH, and USDT directly through traditional exchanges and clearing systems.

However, qualified investors are not subject to such asset limits and trading restrictions.

According to recent reports, the development points out that Russia has taken decisive action to deepen the integration of the crypto market with traditional finance. The debut indicates surging retail interest in cryptocurrency amid regulatory evolution.

It signals a strategic shift in how traditional exchanges handle digital assets. Accommodating retail clients signals growing confidence in the crypto market’s maturity. This highlights rising demand for coordinated exposure to crypto assets within Russia’s capital markets.

The announcement introduces new entry gateways that give retail investors organized access to the crypto market, redefining how these assets are traded locally and internationally.

It has been revealed that in the past, crypto in Russia operated in a highly restrictive, complex regulatory environment. Now, the regulator is moving toward a balance between investor freedom and financial stability. In July, the central bank opened the door to crypto for companies to facilitate global trade. This month, it introduced upcoming legislation that allows retail investors to trade crypto within specified limits.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • While Solana has continued to struggle amid the growing market uncertainty, it appears that traders are increasingly exiting their positions even across its DeFi market.
  • Recent data showcased by blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain shows that two Solana whales unstaked a total of 2.31 million SOL on November 19.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Solana has remained one of the major cryptocurrencies that have been heavily affected by the persistent crypto market volatility, stalling demand from both retail and institutional investors.

While Solana has continued to struggle amid the growing market uncertainty, it appears that traders are increasingly exiting their positions even across its DeFi market.

Recent data showcased by blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain shows that two Solana whales unstaked a total of 2.31 million SOL on November 19.

While the total amount of SOL unstaked was worth about $169.4 million, further data indicated that the whales proceeded to transfer the tokens to Coinbase, a leading cryptocurrency exchange in the U.S.

It is important to note that the act of withdrawing SOL previously committed to the network's staking mechanism is regarded as unstaking.

While this move automatically gives holders the ability to transfer, sell, or use the unstaked tokens, the massive unstaking of 2.31 million SOL from large holders has drawn attention within the crypto community regarding the intention behind the move.

With curiosity on the rise about the whales' decision to move such a large amount of SOL to Coinbase Prime, the timing of the move has triggered speculation that the whales may be intending to sell the tokens.

Notably, the move arrived when Solana was trading around $74, briefly shifting into green territory just a few days after it retested $67, the lowest level seen since June 2026.

Since the prolonged price correction has continued to weaken investor confidence, it appears that the whales have acted upon the growing fear and withdrawn the assets they had initially committed to the Solana network to hedge against further losses.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD unveiled the Yangwang Altior, its new ultra-luxury EV with coach doors, over 1,000 km of CTLC range, a 1,000V fast-charging platform, and plenty of premium extras.

The “super-luxury executive flagship sedan,” as BYD calls it, made its official debut in Abu Dhabi, UAE, over the weekend.

For those who don’t know, Yangwang is BYD’s ultra-luxury sub-brand, sitting at the very top of its brand hierarchy.

The Atrio is Yangwang’s largest and most luxurious sedan, set to compete with high-end brands like Rolls-Royce, Bentley, and Mercedes-Benz Maybach.

Measuring 5,600 mm long, 2,030 mm wide, and 1,590 mm tall, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase, BYD’s flagship sedan sits squarely between the Rolls-Royce Ghost and Phantom (standard wheelbase) in length.

BYD stated the “Golden Body Proportions” are designed to maximize interior space for both front and rear passengers.

Its meticulous front-end design is inspired by “Ding,” a traditional ancient Chinese cauldron, featuring “diamond-cut” headlights, a 137-gemstone dot-matrix grille, and, to top it off, a 24K pure gold car emblem sits up front and center.

The coach doors create a grand entrance, with the front doors opening at an 80-degree angle and the rear doors opening to a 90-degree angle.

Inside, the flagship sedan takes luxury up a notch with a massive, full-length panoramic center infotainment screen that extends from the driver to the passenger side.

The “Wrap-around cockpit” is designed to create an immersive, premium experience, with four executive seats and a central island for rear passengers that includes vehicle controls, storage, and even a champagne glass holder.

In a recent development, BYD said it offers the most second-row space in its class, but didn’t reveal specifics. The zero-gravity “cloud-like” rear seats feature a four-ball mechanical massage head, you know, for those longer trips.

Meanwhile, the front passenger seat can fold at the push of a button to open up more space for rear passengers.

The interior features premium materials, including full-grain genuine leather seats, diamond-cut detailing, real wood trim, and natural lambswool foot pads.

According to recent reports, and that’s not all. It also has a 39-speaker Dynaudio Platinum Evidence high-end sound system that creates an immersive 360-degree “hall-level” sound experience.

The Yangwang Altio is packed with BYD’s latest breakthrough tech, including a high-speed tire-blowout stability system, emergency float mode, and in-place U-turn or tank-turn control using its quad-motor e4 platform.

It's main rival is the Maextro S800, which wasn't in the list.

It also uses BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Fast Charging Technology, which provides a CLTC driving range of over 1,000 km (621 miles).

The flagship sedan features “extremely fast flash charging,” BYD noted, thanks to its 1000V ultra flash charging tech. It takes just five minutes to charge the vehicle’s battery from 10% to 70%. To go from 10% to 97% it takes just nine minutes.

BYD opened orders for the limited-edition “Mountain and River Rhyme” Yangwang Altrio model, which will be extremely exclusive with just 399 units.

Buyers can place a reservation with a 300,000 yuan ($45,000) deposit. BYD didn’t reveal final prices, but the global version is expected to start at around 2 million yuan ($300,000).

  • Fresh research from Grayscale demonstrates Bitcoin’s (BTC) volatility has fallen to roughly 43%—lower than nearly one in five S&P 500 stocks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Is Calmer Than 19% of S&P 500 Stocks, But Here’s a Catch.

Grayscale’s latest report highlights a hidden risk that still catches market-timing investors off guard.

Fresh research from Grayscale demonstrates Bitcoin’s (BTC) volatility has fallen to roughly 43%—lower than nearly one in five S&P 500 stocks.

The catch? Bitcoin’s calmer day-to-day trading hides a massive trap for anyone trying to time dips: almost all of its multi-year gains still come from just a handful of explosive trading days.

In a recent development, in its report, “Beyond Volatility: Rethinking Cryptocurrency Risks,” US digital asset manager Grayscale notes Bitcoin’s long-term performance is heavily influenced by a handful of trading days. Its returns have “fat tails,” meaning sharp gains and losses occur more frequently than in traditional stocks.

Over the past three years, Bitcoin delivered an annualized return of roughly 60%. Excluding its 10 best days would have cut that figure to 7%, while excluding its 10 worst days would have raised it to 197%.

According to recent reports, the report also notes that Bitcoin has historically rebounded sharply after major declines. Since 2011, it has experienced seven drawdowns exceeding 50%, although Grayscale indicates these declines are not unusually severe compared with stocks and bonds when adjusted for volatility.

Grayscale also sees Bitcoin as a potential portfolio diversifier because it is less exposed to traditional market factors.

The company points out that Bitcoin has historically recovered sharply after significant declines. Since 2011, Bitcoin has experienced seven drawdowns of more than 50% from previous highs.

Sources indicate that the report cites Bitcoin’s inclusion in J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions as a milestone.

Grayscale describes JPMorgan as a $5 trillion investment manager that now examines Bitcoin alongside established asset classes.

The banks’ 10-year base case for Bitcoin projects a 10% compound annualized return for Bitcoin over the next decade, the highest among the asset classes covered. The forecast also assumes 55% annualized volatility and a 33% correlation with US large-cap stocks, the number below international equities, corporate bonds and hedge funds.

In Bitcoin’s early years, volatility routinely exceeded 100% and at times approached 200%, with a market cap in the single-digit billions.

Grayscale ties the decline to roughly 43% to larger market value and liquidity, greater institutional participation, Bitcoin exchange-traded products and regulatory clarity.

In historical tests, modest Bitcoin allocations raised annualized return and Sharpe ratio in a representative institutional portfolio.

Over three years, Bitcoin explained about half of return variation across FTSE Grayscale Crypto Sectors. Among the 10 largest non-stablecoin assets, six led quarterly performance over the past two years, while Bitcoin led none.

Industry observers note that JPMorgan’s decision to include Bitcoin in its long-term forecasts, along with declining volatility, could shape how institutions approach crypto investments. At the same time, Grayscale’s data shows how much Bitcoin’s long-term performance depends on a small number of trading days, highlighting the risks of trying to time the market.

#6266. Musk admits Tesla doesn’t have enough talent to build more than one car at a time after exodus

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1731 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Musk admits Tesla doesn’t have enough talent to build more than one car at a time after exodus

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1731 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk now states Tesla can’t build the Cybertruck and the Cybercab at the same time because there are only so many “smart, dedicated people” to go around.
  • It’s the most honest explanation yet for how Tesla went from five consumer vehicle programs at the start of 2026 to a single platform, Model 3 and Model Y, by the middle of 2027.
  • On Friday, Musk stated Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around the middle of next year “to make room for increased Cybercab production.” As we pointed out at the time, Giga Texas isn’t short on space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk now states Tesla can’t build the Cybertruck and the Cybercab at the same time because there are only so many “smart, dedicated people” to go around. Half the executives he showed off in 2023 as proof of Tesla’s “bench strength” have since left the tech giant.

It’s the most honest explanation yet for how Tesla went from five consumer vehicle programs at the start of 2026 to a single platform, Model 3 and Model Y, by the middle of 2027.

On Friday, Musk stated Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around the middle of next year “to make room for increased Cybercab production.” As we pointed out at the time, Giga Texas isn’t short on space. The Cybertruck line runs at a fraction of its installed capacity because the truck sells a fraction of what Tesla planned.

A day later, replying to a user on X, Musk gave a different reason:.

“The biggest thing most people fail to understand is that there are a very limited number of smart, dedicated people! They can only do so many things.”.

He added that if Tesla has to “maintain a complex production line, supply chain and allocate engineering for Cybertruck, we can’t use those people” for scaling Cybercab.

According to recent reports, by this morning, the explanation had shifted again, to the “opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck.” But the Saturday version is the one that matters. Musk is telling us the bottleneck at Tesla isn’t factory space or money. It’s people.

Sources indicate that the Cybertruck is the second casualty this year. In January, Musk announced the end of the Model S and Model X on Tesla’s Q4 earnings call and summed up the reason in one word: “Autonomy.” The Fremont line is being converted to build Optimus robots, and by April, only inventory was left.

According to recent reports, the flagships had been on life support for years. Their last real update was the 2021 interior refresh. The June 2025 “refresh” brought a newly introduced paint color, a front bumper camera, a bit more range, and a $5,000 price increase. That’s not how you treat a vehicle program you care about.

Tesla painted a very different picture just two years ago. At its 2024 shareholder meeting, it showed this slide of its lineup: the Model 3, Model Y, Model S, Model X, Cybertruck, and Semi, plus three vehicles under covers that Musk noted were “going to be pretty special.”.

Of the five consumer vehicles on that slide, three are now dead or on their way out.

So here’s what will be left in the second half of 2027: Model 3 and Model Y, two vehicles built on the same platform, plus the Model Y L and cheaper “Standard” variants of both. The Semi is a commercial truck. The Roadster’s production is still a giant question mark. And the Cybercab is a robotaxi with no steering wheel, not a car you can buy – even though Tesla is going to let fleet buyers get them to add on its own Robotaxi network. We previously explained how this is a terrible idea.

For comparison, Hyundai Motor Group sells more than half a dozen EV models in the US across its Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis brands, on top of its gas and hybrid lineup. GM and Toyota run dozens of nameplates at once. Tesla can’t keep more than two programs alive at the same time.

In a recent development, at Tesla’s Investor Day at Giga Texas on March 1, 2023, Musk mostly stayed out of the spotlight. Instead, Tesla paraded more than a dozen executives on stage to present its intends, a rare move for a company long criticized for being a one-man show.

“We’ve obviously got significant bench strength here,” Musk said at the time.

Of the 14 executives named as presenters that day, seven are gone:.

Martin Viecha, who ran investor relations through that event, left in April 2024 as well.

Seven are still at Tesla, according to their LinkedIn profiles: Tom Zhu, Lars Moravy, Franz von Holzhausen, Ashok Elluswamy, Karn Budhiraj, Laurie Shelby, and Brandon Ehrhart. And the ones who left weren’t peripheral. They ran batteries, powertrain, software, chips, energy, charging, and the money.

The bigger problem for Tesla’s ability to run vehicle programs is the program-level talent, the people who take a car from prototype to volume production.

In a recent development, in November 2025, Tesla lost the head of its Cybertruck program, Siddhant Awasthi, and the Model Y program manager, Emmanuel Lamacchia, within a day of each other. Lamacchia had led Tesla’s best-selling vehicle for four years.

Then the Cybercab, the program Musk is now pulling people toward, started losing its own leaders:.

Add 17-year finance VP Sendil Palani and Thomas Dmytryk, the director who built Tesla’s over-the-air update system and Robotaxi infrastructure, both in March, and you get the picture.

So when Musk states he needs Cybertruck’s people for Cybercab, part of the reason is that Cybercab keeps losing its own.

Musk will frame all of this as focus. Autonomy is going to be so big, the argument goes, that Tesla has to go all in.

But we’ve heard that before. Tesla made the yoke steering wheel standard on the Model S and Model X in 2021 because the cars would soon drive themselves, then brought back a round wheel as an option. It removed the turn signal stalk from the Model 3 in 2023, then brought the stalk back in 2025 and started selling a $350 retrofit to owners. Each time, the autonomy that justified the change wasn’t there yet.

And Tesla isn’t the leader in unsupervised driving. It has the best driver-assist system on the market, but Waymo still logs roughly seven times more driverless miles per week, and NHTSA estimates Tesla’s entire Robotaxi fleet at about 1,000 vehicles. Zoox is scaling too, and Baidu’s Apollo Go runs a far bigger driverless fleet in China.

It has been revealed that this is something that I’ve been highlighting for a decade. Even after it became a major company with a large headcount, Tesla has never been good at running several vehicle programs in a healthy way. The Model S and Model X were starved for updates long before the talent exodus started. Tesla has always thrown everything at its newest program and let the older ones coast.

In a recent development, what changed is that the slack is gone. In 2023, Tesla could still neglect the flagships and keep them on the market, because it had deep benches in engineering, manufacturing, and software to absorb mistakes. Today, half the executives Musk called his bench are gone, and the people running the Cybercab ramp keep walking out. Musk is now openly telling us there aren’t enough people left to build a pickup truck and a robotaxi at the same time.

It has been revealed that musk calls it focus. It looks a lot more like a constraint Tesla can’t hire its way out of.

Tesla never had the capacity to hire, organize, manage and retain the amount of human talent required to develop multiple car model lines in concert. Tesla barely paid its staff enough for one model line development.

You only need to look at other companies with decades of experience in developing many, separate (but technically strongly overlapping) model lines to see how much does that require in terms of human resources and in terms of R&D cost. Like BMW has always been investing ~5 billion EUR every year in R&D. That is how you have ~14 core models with at least another dozen specialist models and more regional models plus Mini and RR on top. At times up to 60 different significant variants with different drivetrains also impacting design, logistics and production. All being always in development for the next generation and also for a mid-life refresh or two. Across the whole group, including maintenance work, there can easily be triple-digit number of vehicle model projects going at the same time.

And Tesla can not even manage a handful.

Industry observers note that will the Cybercab be revolutionary and make it all worth it? We have our doubts. Tesla leads in driver assistance with FSD, but it has failed to evolve the product into unsupervised self-driving at scale, which it promised to buyers for a decade. It’s clearly not the leader in unsupervised self-driving, and the competition is crowded. Tesla’s lasting impact on the robotaxi market is genuinely hard to predict.

According to recent reports, what’s not hard to see is the trend. Tesla has shown a complete inability to sustain multiple vehicle programs at once, and it’s getting harder for the automaker, not easier. If Tesla can’t hold on to the people who build its cars, how long before the Model 3 and Model Y get the same treatment as the Model S?

Both vehicle programs will undoubtedly go down in history as some of the most critical EVs of all time, but that doesn’t guarantee lasting success in a rapidly changing auto landscape.

Industry observers note that the listing comes as Anthropic, the company behind the popular AI chatbot Claude, officially made its much-anticipated stock market debut on Thursday, Nov. 19, with its shares seeing massive volatility.

Industry observers note that as per the latest X post from Coinbase, the exchange announced the availability of Anthropic (ANT) shares for eligible owners in the U.S. and U.K.

In a recent development, it's key to mention that ANT isn't a cryptocurrency but a traditional stock. Coinbase's support for ANT shares reveals the company's efforts to expand its offerings beyond crypto into traditional financial markets.

Anthropic has set a upcoming historic precedent, having successfully raised about $81 billion in its initial public offering (IPO). This is the biggest IPO ever.

The artificial intelligence manufacturer sold 980 million shares at $83 per share, significantly higher than its previously announced price range of $70 to $78.

This brought Anthropic's initial valuation to about $1.5 trillion, making the firm one of the most valuable publicly listed firms in the world right from the get-go.

But as Anthropic shares started trading on the Nasdaq exchange, the ANT ticker saw massive volatility.

In a recent development, as per Reuters, Anthropic shares began trading at $111.50. This represented an enormous 34% premium over the IPO price.

At the initial peak, Anthropic's market cap exceeded $2 trillion, surpassing SpaceX's valuation when it debuted on the market in June.

Anthropic shares slipped to around $95 as the stock gave back a significant chunk of its gains. This was partly due to investors looking to book their profits.

Nonetheless, Anthropic shares were still trading comfortably above their $83 IPO price.

The volatility surrounding Anthropic's stock market debut signals increasing doubts about the AI investment craze.

The listing of Anthropic shares is just one of Coinbase's moves to enter traditional financial markets.

Instead of just providing cryptocurrency trading, the exchange is looking to become a platform for multiple asset classes.

It has been revealed that interestingly, Coinbase had already listed Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual futures for eligible non-U.S. users on Nov. 18.

The perpetual futures were derivative contracts that allowed traders to speculate on Anthropic's valuation before its shares officially started trading on Nasdaq.

Sources indicate that with the latest listing, eligible Coinbase people in the U.S. and U.K. can now trade the publicly listed Anthropic shares.

Anthropic's blockbuster debut comes as financial markets have been rocked by recent volatility, with tech stocks and crypto facing selling pressure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, your electric vehicle battery may last longer than you think. Ford indicates its EV batteries retain greater than 90% health on average after 100,000 miles. Here are a few tips to keep yours healthy.

The Mustang Mach-E went on sale in late 2020 as Ford’s first fully electric crossover SUV designed from the ground up.

Since launching the 2021 Mustang Mach-E, Ford has been collecting data from over 36,000 vehicles that have traveled two billion miles across the US and Canada.

According to Ford, the Mach-E’s battery has retained 92% of its health on average over the past five years.

It has been revealed that across its full EV lineup, including the F-150 Lightning and E-Transit, Ford said its battery packs maintain more than 90% health on average after 100,000 miles. The key number to look at is the spread, with 95% of vehicles falling between 87% and 97% health.

Of 2021 model-year EV owners, Ford stated, more than 2,000 have crossed 100,000 miles with their original battery averaging better than 91% health, while over 30 have crossed the 200,000-mile mark and average 88% health.

Ford is using real-world data to help owners take good care of their electric vehicles, no matter how much they know about batteries and other EV tech.

It’s also applying lessons from developing the Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, which will underpin its next-generation EVs, starting with the Fantom pickup next year.

Industry observers note that ford offered a few simple, everyday tips to help owners support long-term battery health. For one, if possible, charge at home on Level 2 for daily commuting or driving and save DC fast charging for longer trips.

It has been revealed that it also helps to avoid charging in extreme temperatures if you can. Preconditioning the battery can help bring it into the optimal temperature range, while parking in the shade on hot summer days can also help avoid long-term battery degradation.

Last, but not least, you can use the Ford App to find charge-level recommendations designed specifically for your vehicle and battery system.

The 2021 Mustang Mach-E uses an NCM battery, but some newer Ford batteries use a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery chemistry, which is recommended to charge to 100% from time to time.

Ford has introduced new features in the Ford App to help owners maintain battery health specific to their vehicle and will continue to use the data to improve the experience as it introduces its next-gen EVs.

This is an article about Ford EV's, so my comment is kind of relevant.

Recently I picked up a 2017 Ford Focus Electric for my daughter to use when she gets her permit soon. It had 91,000 miles when I got it and now has 92,400 miles. I like driving it enough that I've been driving it and letting my Equinox stay home.

Now, I have no idea how this car has been used or charged since latest (does have the DCFC since it's a 2017). And since it's range was 115 miles factory rated, I have no idea if it's been charged to 100% most or all of the time. What I can tell you is that when I charge it to 100% now, it's giving me about 120 miles on average and I've seen as high as 134 miles. If I turn the A/C on, those numbers drop to 110 on average. Since I live in a mild climate and use the A/C sparingly, my daily commute with mixed driving is giving me a real life 120 to 125 miles.

Not bad for a nearly 10 years old compliance EV!!

Ford will open pre-orders for the Fathom, a midsize electric pickup and first UEV-based model, starting at $28,350 in early 2027.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes the recent crypto market sell-off stems largely from investors rotating capital into high-profile initial public offerings. The Ripple boss and crypto billionaire anticipates a recovery once Anthropic’s massive listing is fully absorbed.

In a recent development, speaking to CNBC on November 19th, Garlinghouse drew a direct parallel to SpaceX’s public debut earlier in the year. He explained that when major IPOs generate intense demand, investors often sell liquid assets such as Bitcoin and XRP to free up cash for share subscriptions.

The same pattern, he noted, unfolded ahead of Anthropic’s offering. After SpaceX completed its listing, crypto markets staged a notable rebound. Garlinghouse expects a similar bounce this time.

Anthropic, the artificial-intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot family, has priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the previously marketed range of $70 to $78.

The deal ranks among the largest IPOs in history, raising tens of billions of dollars and valuing the manufacturer in the trillion-dollar range, and shares are set to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

In a recent development, such blockbuster offerings typically attract enormous institutional and retail interest, temporarily diverting capital from other risk assets. Once the primary allocation is complete and secondary-market trading stabilizes, some of that capital often flows back into crypto and other liquid markets.

Sources indicate that bitcoin had slipped near $62,000 on Wednesday before recovering above $63,000 early Thursday. Garlinghouse framed the dip as a temporary capital-rotation effect rather than a fundamental loss of confidence in digital assets. He also expressed confidence that Anthropic’s shares would trade strongly given the strong demand and pricing above the range.

Looking further ahead, Garlinghouse remained optimistic about blockchain’s long-term role. He predicted that within roughly a decade, blockchain technology will be deeply embedded across global financial infrastructure, much as artificial intelligence has already transformed multiple industries.

His comments highlight how large technology IPOs can create short-term pressure on crypto while potentially reinforcing longer-term narratives around innovation and capital markets.
